name: pb
long: pb is the command line interface for Parseable

children.name: agent
children.short: Show the read-only command catalog for agents
children.example: pb agent -o json

children.name: cloud
children.long: cloud command is used to configure Parseable Cloud access.

children.name: profile
children.long: cloud profile command is used to add Parseable Cloud profiles.

children.name: add
children.long: Add a Parseable Cloud profile using an API key created in Parseable Cloud.
children.example:
pb cloud profile add --api-key psk_xxx
  pb cloud profile add --api-key psk_xxx --name prod

children.name: completion
children.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for pb for the specified shell.
See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.
children.short: Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell

children.name: bash
children.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(pb completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	pb completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/pb

#### macOS:

	pb completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/pb

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.
children.short: Generate the autocompletion script for bash

children.name: fish
children.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the fish shell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	pb completion fish | source

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

	pb completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/pb.fish

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.
children.short: Generate the autocompletion script for fish

children.name: powershell
children.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	pb completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression

To load completions for every new session, add the output of the above command
to your powershell profile.
children.short: Generate the autocompletion script for powershell

children.name: zsh
children.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

	echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(pb completion zsh)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	pb completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_pb"

#### macOS:

	pb completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_pb

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.
children.short: Generate the autocompletion script for zsh

children.name: dataset
children.long: dataset command is used to manage datasets.

children.name: add
children.example:
pb dataset add backend_logs
  pb dataset add frontend_metrics --type metrics
  pb dataset add checkout_traces --type traces

children.name: info
children.example: pb dataset info backend_logs

children.name: list
children.example: pb dataset list

children.name: remove
children.example:
pb dataset remove backend_logs
 pb dataset remove backend_logs --type logs

flags.name: type
flags.usage: Only remove if dataset type matches (logs|metrics|traces)

children.name: schema
children.short: Show dataset field names and types
children.example:
pb dataset schema backend_logs
  pb dataset schema backend_logs -o json

children.name: login
children.long:
Interactive login wizard for Parseable.

Select self-hosted or Parseable Cloud and enter the required
credentials. All settings are saved to ~/.config/pb/config.toml.

children.name: logout
children.short: Logout from the current Parseable profile
children.long: Removes the active profile (URL and credentials) from config.
children.example:
pb logout
  pb logout --yes -o json

children.name: profile
children.long: use profile command to configure different Parseable instances. Each profile takes a URL and credentials.

children.name: add
children.long: Add a new profile to the config file
children.example:
pb profile add local_parseable http://0.0.0.0:8000 admin admin
  pb profile add local_parseable http://0.0.0.0:8000 --api-key psk_xxx

children.name: default
children.short: Set default profile to use with all commands
children.example: pb profile default local_parseable

children.name: list
children.example: pb profile list

children.name: remove
children.example: pb profile remove local_parseable

children.name: update
children.short: Update the URL of an existing profile
children.example: pb profile update local http://localhost:9000

children.name: promql
children.long: Run PromQL queries and explore metrics stored in a Parseable metrics stream.
children.example:
pb promql run -i
  pb promql run "http_requests_total" --dataset otel_metrics --from=1h -i

children.name: active-queries
children.example:
pb promql active-queries
  pb promql active-queries -o json

children.name: cardinality
children.short: Cardinality analysis for a metrics stream
children.long: Analyze label cardinality and active series in a Parseable metrics stream.

children.name: active-series
children.example:
pb promql cardinality active-series otel_metrics '{job="api"}'
  pb promql cardinality active-series --dataset otel_metrics --selector '{job="api"}'

flags.name: limit
flags.usage: Maximum number of series to return

flags.name: lookback
flags.usage: Seconds to look back from now

children.name: label-names
children.short: Labels with the highest number of distinct values
children.example:
pb promql cardinality label-names otel_metrics
  pb promql cardinality label-names --dataset otel_metrics --limit 20

flags.name: limit
flags.usage: Maximum number of labels to return

flags.name: lookback
flags.usage: Seconds to look back from now

children.name: label-values
children.short: Series count per value for a specific label
children.example:
pb promql cardinality label-values otel_metrics service.name
  pb promql cardinality label-values --label job --dataset otel_metrics

flags.name: limit
flags.usage: Maximum number of values to return

flags.name: lookback
flags.usage: Seconds to look back from now

children.name: label-values
children.short: List distinct values for a label
children.example:
pb promql label-values job otel_metrics
  pb promql label-values job --dataset otel_metrics
  pb promql label-values __name__ --dataset otel_metrics

children.name: labels
children.short: List all label names in a metrics stream
children.example:
pb promql labels otel_metrics
  pb promql labels --dataset otel_metrics

children.name: run
children.short: Run a PromQL query (range or instant)
children.long:
Evaluate a PromQL expression against a Parseable metrics stream.
Defaults to range query. Use --instant for point-in-time evaluation.
children.example:
pb promql run "http_requests_total" --dataset otel_metrics --from 1h
  pb promql run "rate(http_requests_total[5m])" --dataset otel_metrics --from 1h --step 1m
  pb promql run "up" --dataset otel_metrics --instant -o json

flags.name: instant
flags.usage: Instant query — evaluate at --to time only

children.name: series
children.short: Find time series matching a label selector
children.example:
pb promql series otel_metrics --match 'http_requests_total'
  pb promql series --match '{job="api"}' --dataset otel_metrics

children.name: tsdb
children.short: Show TSDB statistics for a metrics stream
children.example:
pb promql tsdb otel_metrics
  pb promql tsdb --dataset otel_metrics
  pb promql tsdb --dataset otel_metrics --top 20 --focus-label job

flags.name: date
flags.usage: Date to analyze (YYYY-MM-DD, defaults to today)

flags.name: focus-label
flags.usage: Label to break down series counts by

children.name: role
children.long: role command is used to manage roles.

children.name: add
children.long: Add a new role using an interactive prompt that asks only for its privilege.
children.example: pb role add ingestors

children.name: list
children.example: pb role list

children.name: remove
children.long: Delete an existing role. If the role name is missing, show the available role names without sending a delete request.
children.example:
pb role remove ingestor
  pb role rm ingestor

children.name: sql
children.short: Run SQL query on a dataset
children.long: Run SQL query on a dataset. Default output format is json. Use -i flag to open interactive table view.
children.example:
pb sql run -i
  pb sql run "SELECT * FROM backend" --from=1h -i

children.name: list
children.long: Show the list of saved queries for active user
children.example: pb sql list [-o | --output]

children.name: run
children.short: Run SQL query on a dataset
children.long:
Run SQL query on a dataset. Default output format is text.
Use --output json for JSON output, or -i for interactive table view.
Queries without a SQL LIMIT return at most 500 rows.
Explicit limits are not capped at 500 by pb; choose a reasonable value.
children.example:
pb sql run "select * from frontend" --from=10m --to=now
  pb sql run "select * from frontend" -i

flags.name: save-as
flags.usage: Save this query with a name for later use

children.name: save
children.long: Save a SQL query without running it.
children.example:
pb sql save 'select * from frontend'
  pb sql save "select * from frontend" --name frontend-errors --from=1h --to=now

flags.name: name
flags.usage: Saved query name. Defaults to the dataset name when available.

children.name: status
children.short: Check connection status for the active profile
children.example:
pb status
  pb status -o json

children.name: tail
children.short: Stream live events from a dataset
children.example: pb tail backend_logs

children.name: user
children.long: user command is used to manage users.

children.name: add
children.long: Add a self-hosted user and assign at least one existing role. For Parseable Cloud, invite the user from the dashboard instead.
children.example: pb user add bob --role reader

flags.name: role
flags.usage: specify the role(s) to be assigned to the user. Use comma separated values for multiple roles. Example: --role admin,developer

children.name: list
children.example: pb user list

children.name: remove
children.example: pb user remove bob

children.name: set-role
children.long: Add one or more roles to a user without removing their existing role assignments.
children.example: pb user set-role bob admin,developer

children.name: version
children.long: Print the client version. For server and connection details, use pb status.
children.example: pb version
